questions.subject: Generative AI
questions.question: Explain the difference between GANs and diffusion models in Generative AI.
questions.ideal_answer: GANs and diffusion models differ in several ways: GANs is generative adversarial networks (works by generator-discriminator game) whereas diffusion models is iterative denoising generation (works by reverse diffusion process). GANs is typically used for minimax objective, Nash equilibrium, while diffusion models is used for DDPM, DDIM, Stable Diffusion. Example demonstrating GANs: DCGAN, StyleGAN, CycleGAN. Example demonstrating diffusion models: noise schedule, U-Net architecture.

questions.question: What is VAE in Generative AI and how does it work?
questions.ideal_answer: VAE in Generative AI refers to variational autoencoder. It works by latent space generative model. Key characteristics include reparameterization trick, KL divergence. Example: encoder: q(z|x), decoder: p(x|z). Common pitfalls include blurry outputs vs GANs.

questions.question: What is flow-based models in Generative AI and how does it work?
